title: Northbeam Returns and Restocking: Authorising a Return and Bringing the Item Back
content:
A return is authorised, and a label or collection issued, only while the authorisation stands in requested or authorized. The way the item comes back is one the schedule allows, and where the customer asks for a way it does not allow the nearest allowed way is offered instead. *A prepaid label stays usable for the schedule's label validity days from the day it is issued, and an expired label is reissued once without a fee* — that clause is **no longer in force**, having been superseded for Northbeam Returns and Restocking by the current basis on which the days a booking is held open are settled. *a collection needs the schedule's lead days of notice and may be moved only as often as the schedule allows* — this clause is likewise **no longer in force**, superseded by the current basis on which the notice for a collection is settled. Where the customer pays the return shipping the carrier fee of the schedule is charged, and where the item is graded defective on arrival that fee is refunded with the line. A palletised business return is collected on freight at the freight fee of the schedule, and the business authorisation the schedule requires is on file before the crew is booked. An item damaged on the way back is settled against whoever the schedule's liability basis names, and the customer is not refused the refund while that is worked out.

## The state the authorisation must stand in

An authorisation may be authorised, and a label or collection issued against it, only while its status is requested or authorized. The status is read from the return authorisation record identified by its own reference number, not from what the customer believes the return's position to be, and it is read before the authorisation or the issue is made.

| Status of the authorisation | May it be authorised, or a label or collection issued? |
| --- | --- |
| requested | yes |
| authorized | yes |
| in transit | no |
| received | no |
| inspected | no |
| settled | no |
| denied | no |
| withdrawn | no |

## The route back, and the charges on it

- The way the item comes back is one the schedule allows. Where the customer asks for a way the schedule does not allow, the nearest allowed way is offered instead.
- Where the customer pays the return shipping, the carrier fee of the schedule is charged. Where the item is then graded defective on arrival, that fee is refunded with the line.
- A palletised business return is collected on freight, at the freight fee of the schedule.
- The business authorisation the schedule requires is on file before the crew is booked.
- An item damaged on the way back is settled against whoever the schedule's liability basis names. The customer is not refused the refund while that is worked out.

## Two situations the clauses in force decide, on hypothetical facts

*A customer on a schedule allowing only in-store drop-off asks for a carrier to call.* The nearest allowed way is offered instead, which on that schedule is the drop-off at the counter.

*A customer pays the carrier fee of their schedule, and the bench then grades the item defective on arrival.* The fee is refunded with the line.
